# Arithmetic/global retrospective: what still has room

2026-09-30. Independent retrospective after registry110, deliberately pausing the current ordinary scalar calculation. No proposal below is a theorem or a claimed OC resolution. Source names are relative to `work/`.

## 1. The global skeleton is substantially stronger than the local numerical tools

The following is the most useful assembled starting point.

1. `candidate 2086e4eaa4bce465`, Sections5--6, and `candidate c280bb0dcfd30f3d` reduce an actual positive-volume counterexample to an attained, positive, dependence-connected canonical family. The lift retains ALL anchored representations and every pairwise integer congruence, in particular the original occupied parity count k<=2^n. Dependence components have disjoint parity classes. This is an actual compact reduction; unrestricted finite bases and projective changes are inadmissible.
2. `candidate 4a38a3cfd6733dce` fixes at most k(I) witnesses of the ACTUAL deepest-base set I before any critical circuits are selected. Any critical circuit at each witness covers its assigned deepest face. This solves the witness-count quantifier, not coverage of all measured fibers.
3. `candidate a68c14b477a24d06`, `candidate 7278f286325c46c7`, and `candidate 7127f9c7b67df7cb` retain actual boundary motion, both base and continuous barycenters, normals, and the relevant facet branches. At an admissible minimum the remaining problem really is a geometric restriction on a boundary transport/profile, not absence of a formal Farkas system.

I would use this attained global skeleton as the organizing framework. The number of proved ordinary inequalities has grown much faster than the number of mechanisms that connect their different fibers. Another unrestricted simplex inequality, by itself, does not fill that interface.

## 2. Failure map: information that cannot be discarded again

**Helly and lattice-free grouping.** `candidate a222e8a47d0c28ff` already gives the stronger M/2^n budget when original caps capture whole fibers. The hard part is partial continuous traces. `candidate d0f838592db846be` retains actual convex fibers, full-parity witnesses, strict facet contacts, and positive circuits, but its basin inequality max cap >=Gamma times basin mass is false. A new grouping claim must use genuine low-depth/global-critical hypotheses or additional joint geometry. The lattice-free-container notes also retain a real outer-boundary flux: it can carry ALL relevant mixed measure and cannot be removed by ordinary-volume approximation.

**Mass quotas and finite-fiber induction.** `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)` exactly characterizes fractional proper-minor parity covers: they exist precisely when there is a nontrivial closed partition into unions of whole parity classes. The thirteen-point canonical base has no such partition and has compatible strictly quota-feasible volumes. Thus improving the linear program over the SAME mass quotas cannot help. Conversely `candidate 6d98cff7cbcfe25c` pays those particular volumes for arbitrary shapes, so this arithmetic obstruction is not geometric impossibility.

**Midpoint transport and scalar packet allocation.** The sharp parity density contraction is proved, but its factor2^n can occur at one fiber. The iterated consensus has at most2^n actual limiting points, yet ALL of them fail the target in `candidate 233dacf87d7f01e6`. The seven-fiber density-envelope obstruction and the actual (1/4,1,1) residual-credit obstruction exclude universal closure by total density, masses, or independently packed barycentric relations. The missing information is directional coincidence among actual endpoint caps, not just a better scalar constant.

**Rounding and thin/wide.** Exact arithmetic zonotope coefficients and the certified-rounding criterion survive. But `candidate 083bddf65bb5abc1` has C=conv(S), equal positive nonheavy fibers, and unbounded projection coefficients after EVERY shear and primitive-direction choice. The obstruction is hollow-face nonaffine drift. The exact extrusion relocation example also shows that every OLD center can fail after one extrusion. There is no viable global scalar coefficient dichotomy currently.

**Potential selection.** A PRESCRIBED regular critical profile can have full convex-potential efficiency below Gamma, even with completeness and strict count quotas: R4 has exact efficiency40/93<4/9. It is nevertheless far above OC's depth threshold and has a different paying circuit. `candidate 0c18dc829db98d22` rules out the separate assumption that all critical caps at all deepest points cover S, even with strict nonheaviness in its three-disk example. These are different obstructions and neither refutes favorable circuit selection at a bad attained minimum.

## 3. First priority: selected circuits plus the ACTUAL contact-capacity poset

**Surviving tools.** The finite response polytope

    theta>=0, sum theta=1, sum theta_j S_j u_j=0

and its exact LP dual are proved in `candidate b1ef83513bdb0bcf`. Extremes use at most d+1 rows. `candidate 810352ec6ea27062` turns an unpayable high-profile vertex into simultaneous anchored equality in all incident support offsets. The newest `candidate 6eda5637cc09a539` gives an exact submeasure-transport certificate and confines each transition to its ACTUAL lower-support-graph face. Destination capacity on shared subfaces is counted only once.

**Why this has more room than old individual-efficiency claims.** The variables are the critical menu, its response weights, and the current face capacities together. R4 fixes a bad menu; its alternative orbit pays. A perturbation that destroys its shared contacts exposes a paying hinge. Thus a false universal prescribed-profile inequality is not the right adversary for this joint problem.

**Decisive missing step.** At a bad attained minimum, prove either a favorable selected circuit exists or the entire obstructing transport reduces to a proper canonical minor/affine-contact block whose original mass pays by restriction. The unrestricted statement is theorem-strength and must be labeled so. The smaller next question should be a contact propagation lemma, not that full assertion.

**Concrete first lemma to test.** For common-normal simplex fibers on a primitive chain, fix a finite complete regular critical menu at an interior deepest source. Follow a high-profile vertex through its exact common-contact intervals. Does maximal propagation either reach an exposed paying endpoint or produce one interval on which ALL support offsets are affine and whose same selected response is paid by an endpoint radial potential? Treat cap boundaries and the endpoint response weights explicitly. In rank one the contact cells are intervals; in higher rank they meet on a face poset and the next obstruction becomes visible. This is narrower than OC and not settled by the existing affine-centroid theorem: only some incident offsets are initially affine, and the selected cap slopes need not agree.

**Mandatory tests.** The original R4 bad menu must be allowed to fail until the menu changes. The crosspolytope construction in Section6 below prevents assuming that separate vertex-type contacts automatically amalgamate in higher rank. Uniform source-fixing Markov contractions are already rigid automorphisms and cannot be substituted for this propagation.

## 4. Second priority: cap-signature-aware induction, not another mass allocation

**Surviving tools.** Proper-minor quotas, the attained residual-root program with its exact KKT martingale, and all-status anchored residual credit are established. The functional injection `candidate c2528b1460a23da4` additionally preserves ANY monotone Boolean profile of simultaneous missed caps against ONE actual baseline. It retains overlap information that the scalar root program loses.

**Proposed new object.** For a fixed finite critical menu keep the full table

    m_p(J)=|K_p intersect intersection_(j in J) H_j^c|,

rather than only the smallest residual after at most t caps. Each column comes from an actual convex intersection and has root-concave interpolation. The columns also obey exact inclusion/exclusion and monotone-profile injection inequalities on the SAME bodies. Treat the table and a shared allocation as one finite feasibility problem; do not optimize columns independently.

**Small decisive first lemma.** Use TWO anchored relations sharing a source fiber, one common target, and THREE actual caps. Glue their actual couplings conditionally on the shared source, and retain its full three-bit cap signature. Derive a joint inequality for the two induced target residual laws that charges the shared captured source mass only once. The existing one-baseline functional injection does NOT already give this: its disjoint images cannot simply be added across different baselines. A success would add one precise cross-relation constraint to the KKT program; an exact compatible counterexample would close this proposed gain. Start with a finite incidence certificate and actual shared marginals, not a global packing assertion.

**What eventual assembly must prove.** A parity-bounded family of these joint certificates must price overlaps without charging the same fiber or shared face twice. Merely asserting that the enriched LP is infeasible below Gamma/k would again be equivalent in strength to the missing global theorem. The first lemma above is a genuine intermediate test because it concerns one relation and one specified cap triple.

**Mandatory obstructions.** The seven-fiber scalar-envelope example; the (1/4,1,1) exact residual-credit failure; and the parity forest whose transported copies coincide. All three retain the right marginal quantities, so none is repaired by reusing their totals with new notation.

## 5. A conditional fallback: contact-rank descent instead of universal quantitative stability

The archived BM-tight centroid-graph theorem pays families once the relevant midpoint inclusions are tight. `candidate e4ccf81294305ade` gives an exact dominated measure and exact directional control of centroid displacement by actual Minkowski surplus. However the paired-tail examples show that a deficit can be higher order than, and not linearly payable by, that volume surplus. The nonaffine reflection plateaus also disprove strict improvement from translations alone.

A more plausible structural use is QUALITATIVE at an attained minimum: choose an auxiliary extremum of active support/contact rank, and show that a slack anchored relation permits a compatible deformation which preserves the minimal depth value while reducing that rank, or strictly improves the normalized depth. This would avoid demanding a false uniform linear surplus bound.

The small test is a leaf of the ACTIVE anchored-representation/contact hypergraph: only one anchored inclusion uses the movable fiber in the selected support directions. Apply the already proved exact contraction/quantile response, including full/empty facets and competing source switches, and ask whether a nontrivial slack leaf can persist at a lexicographically minimal bad family. A theorem here would be useful in every integer rank. It must not be presented as an arbitrary-graph induction: the thirteen-point indecomposable base and flat translation plateaus are explicit checks on that jump.

## 6. Out-of-box test A: coupled base/continuous symmetries

Existing paying orbit theorems preserve EVERY individual fiber and require an affine centroid graph (or a direction annihilated by its defect). They do not cover a finite symmetry that PERMUTES unequal fibers while acting on continuous coordinates. This is a concrete different source of favorable circuits.

Test the following actual family in arbitrary d>=2. Let T have barycentric coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_d and vertices v_i. Put n=d+1,

    P={0,+/-e_0,...,+/-e_d},
    K_0=T,
    K_(+e_i)=K_(-e_i)=epsilon v_i+(1-epsilon)T,
                         0<epsilon<1.

The base is lattice-complete. Its only nontrivial interior integer site is0; every convex combination at0 lies in T, so the hull has exactly these fibers. The center graph is nonaffine: the two endpoints on axis i have the same shifted centroid, different from g_T. Simultaneous axis permutations and vertex permutations preserve the body and fix (0,g_T); independent base sign changes do too. Thus this lies outside the individual-fiber symmetry theorem while retaining a large explicit finite group.

This is only a contact/symmetry calibration: n=d+1>=3 and |P|=2n+1<=2^n, so a largest fiber already pays OC by its ordinary centroid. It is not a nonheavy bad-depth model.

At the central type-j vertex, both endpoints +/-e_j give a common contact relation for every incident offset lambda_i, i!=j. Different vertex types use different axes. There need be no nontrivial representation preserving ALL d+1 offsets. Thus this also tests the precise non-amalgamation issue in Section3.

**First lemma:** characterize the response profile of the FULL coupled symmetry orbit of one genuine regular critical cap at(0,g_T), and prove or refute Gamma-paying potential selection for that orbit. Do not assume its base tilt stays fixed: it does not. An exact failure would be informative; success would yield a new all-rank selection class with nonaffine centers and suggest the correct orbit-average arithmetic credit.

## 7. Out-of-box test B: layer-dependent Doignon certificates with ONE joint cost

The exact no-slicing theorem and convex residual-root superlevels suggest integrating certificates across residual levels rather than fixing one affine majorant and then losing its worst error. The archived approximate-cover theorem and KKT program already solve the fixed-threshold version. The new question is whether level changes can be coordinated by the actual cap-signature table of Section4.

**First lemma:** for a finite menu and one fixed affine positive scale ell(p), let the Doignon witnesses for

    |(C intersect intersection_(j in J) H_j^c)_p|^(1/d)
                                      > t ell(p)

vary with t. Prove an exact finite layer-cake dual in which the integrated original-cap weights are charged ONCE, and identify the additional compatibility condition needed for its total cost to improve on the old fixed-threshold bound. This is a finite Farkas/integration problem before any universal numerical claim. If the optimum is exactly the existing convex residual program, prove that equivalence and close the idea immediately. If it is stronger, test the actual small counterexamples before attempting parity assembly.

This proposal is deliberately falsifiable: it may merely recover the old program. A layer-cake identity alone is not a new mechanism, and no claim of a Gamma budget follows without the strict comparison.

## Recommendation

Prioritize joint critical-menu/contact-capacity geometry, with the coupled-symmetry family as a clean independent calibration. Keep a second route on actual joint residual signatures and overlap accounting. Use the contact-rank leaf problem only if an actual feasible deformation can be specified. Do not restart unqualified centroid rounding, parity consensus, coefficient-large inference, single-template cores, or prescribed-profile Gamma claims; their exact counterexamples already retain the commonly proposed extra hypotheses.

All proposed full-rank conclusions still require the nonsmooth allocation/variation interface and the intrinsic lower-dimensional reduction at the end. No statement here silently changes H_q to full d-volume. The exploratory sources above mostly use q=d; that scope remains explicit.
